subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: Should Telegram voice/message ingress add a source message timestamp-to-dispatch latency watchdog and a direct-message visible fallback for aborted/no-final turns, and what thresholds/text should it use?
rationale: The code gap is real, but restart thresholds and visible fallback semantics can affect message delivery behavior and need maintainer intent before an automated repair changes user-visible Telegram flows.

options.title: Define narrow watchdog and fallback
options.body: Approve a bounded Telegram fix that measures Telegram message.date against dispatch time, records account/chat/message/media diagnostics, and emits a clear direct-message fallback for aborted no-final voice turns.

options.title: Split polling and reply work
options.body: Keep polling liveness PR work separate from the voice fallback/delivery issue and require two smaller reviewed fixes with separate live proof.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Do not change behavior until a maintainer or reporter reproduces the exact 14-minute delay and abort/no-reply sequence on current main.

recommendation.title: Define narrow watchdog and fallback
recommendation.body: Approve a bounded Telegram fix that measures Telegram message.date against dispatch time, records account/chat/message/media diagnostics, and emits a clear direct-message fallback for aborted no-final voice turns.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter split the polling liveness helper and is the best available routing candidate for the watchdog/fallback policy choice among the sampled history owners.
